## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Gym scene wiring (CG-0MPFM2MM4003OPP8).
- Parent: Suppress shared Gym help chrome in pure scene-only SLL views (CG-0MPFLM5EB009N5X8).

Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

data.description:
# Release gate marks a retry-accepted stage as FAIL (exit 0, `outcome=retry-clean`)

## Summary

`scripts/run_tests.py` harvests failure names from a stage's **combined output**
(`parse_failures`) even when the stage's own retry runner already discarded the
failing attempt and returned **exit 0**. A `retry-clean` stage is therefore
reported as a suite failure, so the dev→main release gate blocks a genuinely
green tree.

Observed during the v0.1.24 release (merged tree, load ~7):

```
all: FAIL [full scope] [type full] [full lane] (npm --silent test)
  facts: elapsed=300.35s, slot_wait=0.00s, lane=full, exit_code=0, configured_timeout=1500s, command=npm --silent test
  FAILED: tests/core-engine/tf-runtime-integration.browser.test.ts
Release script exited with code 1.
```

while the stage's own output records:

```
FAIL  |browser (chromium)| tests/core-engine/tf-runtime-integration.browser.test.ts
Error: Failed to import test file .../tf-runtime-integration.browser.test.ts
Caused by: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:63315/...
[retry] Vitest transient failure (worker RPC timeout, browser connection drop, or module fetch failure) detected with no attributable test failure. Retrying once...
 ✓ |browser (chromium)| tests/core-engine/tf-runtime-integration.browser.test.ts (3 tests) 162ms
 Test Files  44 passed (44)
[vitest-runner] attempts=2 status=0 outcome=retry-clean args="--project browser" expected=44 ran=44
```

The unit stage in the same run was clean (`241/241` files, `3870` tests,
`outcome=clean`), and `npm --silent test` exited **0**.

## Goal (user story)

As a release engineer, I want a stage the project's own retry runner accepted
(`outcome=retry-clean` / `outcome=transient-accepted`) to be reported green, so a
contention flake that the runner already recovered does not block a release whose
code is sound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When a stage's final `[vitest-runner] ... status=0 outcome=retry-clean` (or
      `transient-accepted`) verdict is present, `parse_failures` discards failure
      names harvested from the superseded attempt and the suite reports success.
- [ ] The documented masking guards are unchanged: a stage whose retry ends
      `outcome=retry-failed` / `outcome=failed`, or a stage with no retry banner,
      still reports every genuine failure.
- [ ] The discarded-attempt failures remain visible as diagnostics (not as suite
      failures) so an operator can still see which file flaked.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: retry-clean output with a failed first attempt (green),
      retry-failed output (red, failures listed), and genuine-failure-only output
      (red, unchanged).
- [ ] The release gate (`scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` → `run_tests.py
      --scope full`) no longer needs a re-run after an accepted retry.

## Evidence

- Cache entry: `.worklog/cache/ce0b22f933c88660bc44ee97bca48193`
  (`exit_code: 0`; stdout carries both the failed attempt and
  `outcome=retry-clean`).
- Release log: `/tmp/ship-release-20261113-042438.log`.

Discovered during the v0.1.24 release (`/skill:ship release`).
data.title: Test skill: run_tests.py reports a retry-accepted stage as FAIL (exit 0, outcome=retry-clean)
